Person.comment:
Ron Caspi received his PhD in Marine Microbiology in 1996 from the Scripps Institution of Oceanography in La Jolla, CA, under the guidance of Dr. Bradley Tebo and Dr. Margo Haygood. He completed his post-graduate education in 1999 with Dr. Donald Helinski at the Center for Molecular Genetics at UC San Diego.

After three years with Pangene Corporation, where he managed the automation and bioinformatics department, Ron joined SRI International in 2004, and has been the head curator of the MetaCyc database ever since.

Protein.comment:
The acetyl-CoA decarbonylase/synthase complex (ACDS) is an important enzyme in the methanogenesis pathway from acetate. It cleaves the C-C and C-S bonds in the acetyl moiety of acetyl-CoA, oxidizes the carbonyl group to CO2 and transfers the methyl group to tetrahydrosarcinapterin. The enzyme can also catalyze the synthesis of acetyl-CoA, a reaction that is not used in methanogenesis, but in autotrophic growth on one-carbon substrates [Terlesky86, Terlesky87, Abbanat90, Ferry92, MaupinFurlow96].

This large (~2000 kDa) complex is composed of three enzyme components and five different subunits, with a structure of (α2ε2)4(β)8(γδ)8.

The β subunit contains a binuclear Ni-Ni center bridged by a cysteine thiolate to an [Fe4S4] cluster [Kocsis99, Gencic03, Gu03a, Funk04], and the γδ component contains a corrinoid/iron-sulfur cofactor [MaupinFurlow96a].

Several partial reactions were correlated with specific components of the complex [Grahame96]: CO dehydrogenase activity (EC 1.2.7.4) is catalyzed by the αε component [Gong08, Balbo03], carbon monoxide-methylating acetyl-CoA synthase activity (EC 2.3.1.169) is catalyzed by the β subunit, and the rapid, reversible transfer of a methyl group between the γδ component's corrinoid cofactor and tetrahydrosarcinapterin (EC 2.1.1.245) is catalyzed by the γδ component.

The enzyme components and the reactions catalyzed by them are similar to the carbon monoxide dehydrogenase/acetyl-CoA synthase enzyme system, which is used for anaerobic oxidation of acetate by anaerobic bacteria and for de novo synthesis of acetyl groups in autotrophic species and acetogens. However, that system includes several individual enzymes that, unlike ACDS, are isolated separately and not present in the form of a high molecular mass complex [Gencic10].
